prompt_arguments: local-full gpt2 "Given a sentence like 'When Mary and John went to the store, John gave a drink to', GPT-2 small continues with ' Mary' rather than ' John'. How does it work out which name to output? The dataset task is 'ioi'." budget=60 investigation=ioi
scientist: Claude Code (headless, subscription), MCP tools only
final_message:
**Status: verified.** All results came from `local-full` (fp32). V0002 passed every check on held-out inputs (ioi seed 777, n=200). I used 30 of the 60 experiments.

**How it works.** GPT-2 finds the name that appears twice and outputs the other one:
1. **Spot the repeat (at the second mention of the subject).** Head 3.0 looks back from that mention to the earlier copy of the same name. Head 5.5 looks at the token right after the earlier copy. Head 6.9 also contributes (E0009, E0012).
2. **Carry the signal to the end.** Heads 7.3, 7.9, 8.6 and 8.10 attend from the last token back to the repeated name. They bring "this name was repeated" forward during layers 7-8 (E0005, E0008).
3. **Copy the other name.** That signal sets what heads 9.9, 9.6 and 10.0 look for (E0011). They attend to the name that wasn't repeated and copy it into the output; 9.9 alone contributes +3.0 to the logit difference. Swapping which name is repeated flips their attention, so they follow the repetition, not the position (E0020).
4. **Counterweight.** Heads 10.7 and 11.10 attend to the same name but push against it (−2.0 and −0.8).

As code: `return the one of the first two names that doesn't appear again`, which matches the model on 93.5% of held-out prompts. Every mismatch is the model saying " the", " her" or " his" instead of a name.

**Verification numbers (V0002, circuit of 23 heads plus MLPs 0-6):**

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Agreement with the model | 0.935 |
| Circuit ablated | logit diff −13% of clean (accuracy 0) |
| Circuit alone | logit diff 99% of clean, but top-1 accuracy only 0.375 |
| Random ablations of the same size | 104-106% |

**What didn't hold:**
- **Name movers aren't the bottleneck.** Removing them keeps 83% of the effect, because backup heads spread across layers 9-11 take over (E0013, E0016, E0019). The real bottleneck is the layer 7-8 heads: ablating those four leaves 12% (E0023).
- **My first circuit failed.** With 14 heads plus MLP 0 (V0001), the circuit on its own gave −10%. It passed after adding nine supporting heads plus MLPs 1-6.
- **MLPs 1-6 are only background machinery.** They're needed for the circuit to run on its own, but carry no task-specific information. Ablating just the 23 heads, with all MLPs intact, reverses the model's preference (E0030).

**Limitations:**
- **Not the whole behaviour.** The circuit explains why the model prefers the right name over the repeated one, not why it outputs a name at all (that 0.375 top-1 accuracy).
- **One sentence template.** Only the "When A and B went to the P, C gave a O to" form was tested.
- **Backup heads located only by layer.** The tool's direct logit attribution ignored my ablation parameter (E0017), so I couldn't name the individual backup heads.
- **One test was inconclusive.** E0025 couldn't tell what feeds head 5.5, because of how the experiment was designed.

**Report:** `benchmarks\ioi\report\report.md` (plus `report.html` in the same folder). The report's status line reads "partial / not verified · verified". That's because the failed V0001 is still on file; the verified circuit is V0002.

I couldn't run the vault search at the start or save a method note at the end, because this session has no shell or file access.
